purpose: Solifenacin is used to treat overactive bladder (OAB). It helps reduce symptoms like sudden strong urges to urinate, needing to urinate too often, and accidental leakage of urine. It helps you feel more in control of your bladder throughout the day.
how_it_works: Your bladder has muscle receptors that can sometimes overreact and cause sudden, uncontrollable urges to urinate. Solifenacin works by blocking these receptors, called muscarinic receptors, which helps calm and relax the bladder muscle. This means your bladder can hold more urine and you feel less of those sudden urgent urges.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is dry mouth, so sipping water throughout the day can help. You may also notice constipation, blurry vision, dry eyes, or feeling drowsy. Some people experience difficulty fully emptying their bladder or an upset stomach.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, kidney or liver problems, or trouble urinating, as this medication may not be safe for you. Because it can cause drowsiness and blurry vision, be careful when driving or using machinery. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated, especially in hot weather, since this medication can reduce sweating. Older adults should use this medication with caution as it may affect memory or cause confusion.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one 5 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed and if you tolerate it well. Always take it at the same time each day and swallow the tablet whole.
